speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that. To begin our assessment, how long have you been experiencing these diarrhea symptoms, and have there been any episodes of fever or severe abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has your stool been associated with blood or mucus, and do you notice any blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Stool_Occult_Blood. REQUEST TEST: C. diff_Toxigenesis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, no recent antibiotics usage apart from levofloxacin for pneumonia, no vomiting, no blood in stool. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-Associated Clostridioides difficile Infection (CDI). The clinical picture of recent levofloxacin use followed by acute watery diarrhea without fever or bloody stool is classic for CDI. We must await the C. diff toxin results to confirm, but treatment with oral vancomycin is indicated immediately.
